text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government is optimistic about achieving its 10-million 375-lb bale production target in 1996/97 (July-June).
- The government is losing millions of rupees due to tyre smuggling from neighbouring Afghanistan to Pakistan.
- The Ministry of Food and Agriculture is likely to take up the issue of massive smuggling of wheat to Afghanistan from Pakistan.
- Indonesia and Pakistan have signed a memorandum of understanding on promoting shipbuilding and ship repairs.
- The state-run Pakistan International Airlines will raise fares between five and 10 percent from October 1.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan has denied rumours about freezing of foreign currency deposit accounts.
- The rupee slipped by 70 paisa against the dollar in the kerb market and closed at 41 to the dollar on Monday.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto has said direct foreign investment reached $3.1 billion in the last three years.
- Pakistan has granted traffic rights to KLM, Emirates and Gulf Air airlines to operate to and from Lahore and Islamabad.
- U.N. under-secretary general for political affairs, Marrack Goulding, has denied Pakistan's involvement in Afghan fighting.
- Pakistan will sign an extradition treaty with the United States.
- The Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry has opposed the government's policy of exporting raw cotton instead of concentrating on export of value-added cotton products.
